body: Ganoderma lucidum, dried and milled into a vegan capsule. The listing prints it as 100 per cent reishi and names nothing else alongside it.
What it does not print is which part of the fungus that is. The bracket and the mycelium are both sold as reishi powder, and this label does not choose between them.
Two capsules a day, with breakfast or lunch, and at least 500 ml of water.
Two is the serving. If you miss a day, take two the next morning rather than four.

body: Which part of the fungus is in the capsule, an extraction ratio, and where it was grown or gathered. None of the three is on the current label, so none of them is on this page.
The count and the milligrams are printed, which is why there is a cost a day here and none on the chaga.
Somewhere dry, out of direct sun, with the lid on. A capsule needs no fridge and no cold chain, which is the one practical difference between this and a gel.
Anyone who reacts to mushrooms should leave it alone. This is a fungus, milled and put into a capsule, and it is an allergen for some people.
If you take medication that thins the blood, ask your GP or pharmacist first. If you are pregnant or nursing, or you take prescribed medication, ask before you start. It is not for children.
Sent out from 599 Smithdown Road, Liverpool, Tuesday to Sunday. UK delivery is free over £50, or you can collect from the shop between 10 and 6, any day except Monday.

ingredients.intro: The listing names one ingredient and one only. Here is the organism, what dried reishi looks like, and the question about it that our label does not yet answer.

cards.alt: Ganoderma lucidum growing on dead hardwood
cards.p: A bracket fungus of dead and dying hardwood, oak and plum among them. The cap is kidney shaped and varnished, red brown over a pale rim, and it grows hard rather than fleshy. Nobody eats it off a plate. Lingzhi is the Chinese name and reishi the Japanese one, and both are a good deal older than the jar.

cards.latin: Which part is in the jar
cards.p: Reishi is sold as the bracket, dried and milled, and it is also sold as mycelium grown on grain. Ours does not say which, so this page does not say either. The slices in the photograph are the bracket. Whether that is what stands behind the 800 mg is a question for the label, and the label has not answered it.

cards.alt: Plain capsules and a wooden scoop on a slate board, a generated scene
cards.p: The powder goes into a vegan capsule. The shell material is not named on the current label, so it is not named on the sheet below either. The capsules in the picture are a generated scene rather than a photograph of ours.

spec.intro: Everything we can tell you about what is in the jar, including the one line we cannot fill in yet and why.
spec.caption: Reishi Capsules
rows: One ingredient. Ganoderma lucidum, dried and milled, in a vegan capsule. The listing prints it as 100 per cent reishi.
Ganoderma lucidum, family Ganodermataceae. Sold in English as reishi, in Chinese as lingzhi. The current listing spells the second word Ganordema; the accepted binomial is the one printed here.
Not printed. The label does not say whether the powder is the bracket or mycelium grown on grain, so neither do we. Why that line is worth having is set out in the mushroom label article.
None declared. The listing names one ingredient and the capsule, and no grain, bulking agent or flow agent.
Vegan. The shell material is not named on the current label, so we do not state it here. Mycrodose names its shell as hydroxypropyl methylcellulose; this jar does not.
50 capsules at 800 mg each, as printed.
None printed. The listing does not sell this as a concentrated extract, and a ratio invented for a label is worse than no ratio at all. Chaga is the jar on this shelf that says extract.
Not printed. We are not going to name a country we cannot evidence.
£24.99. One size. 50 capsules at two a day is 25 days, which works out at £1 a day.
Two capsules daily, with breakfast or lunch, and at least 500 ml of water. The listing says spring water.
Dry, out of direct sun, lid on. It does not need a fridge.

Anyone who reacts to mushrooms. If you take medication that thins the blood, ask your GP or pharmacist first, because reishi is one of the botanicals routinely flagged for that. Not for children. If you are pregnant or nursing, or you take prescribed medication, ask before you start.
spec.smallprint: Contains mushroom, which is an allergen for some people. Do not exceed the stated dose. Speak to your GP or pharmacist before starting any supplement, particularly if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or take medication. Food supplements should not be used as a substitute for a varied and balanced diet and a healthy lifestyle. Keep out of reach of young children.

doctrine.h3: We publish the specification. We do not publish claims about what it does.
doctrine.p: The species is named in Latin, the count and the milligrams are printed, the serving is printed, and the one line we cannot fill in, which part of the fungus is in the jar, sits on the sheet as a blank rather than a guess. What reishi does in a person is not something we are permitted to say, so it is not on this page.

reiss.label: Reiss's turn
paras: I sell a lion's mane that says fruiting body on the label, and I have written a whole article about why that phrase is worth the trouble. Then there is this jar, which says reishi, 100 per cent, 800 mg, and stops. It does not say which part of the fungus that is.

I could guess. Reishi has been dried and milled as the bracket for a very long time, and that is what most of the trade means by the word. But a guess in a specification is a lie with good manners, so the sheet above carries a blank instead, and the blank stays until the label answers it.

Everything else here is printed and can be checked: the species, the count, the milligrams, the serving, the price. One line is missing. I would rather you knew which line than found out later that nobody had told you.
reiss.pull: A guess in a specification is a lie with good manners.
